text:
I visited Dr. Prasit's practice because of problems with my left ear, and I can only say: I highly recommend him.

For over a week, I'd been experiencing discomfort—my ear was constantly moist, fluid was leaking, and I had an unpleasant pressure sensation, similar to what you feel on an airplane. I also kept hearing a popping sound in my ear.

I arrived at the practice shortly before 5:00 p.m., even though appointments don't start until 5:00 p.m. At that time, there were already over 20 patients waiting. After checking in, I was kindly told to come back around 7:00 p.m. This worked perfectly: I didn't have to wait even five minutes and was seen immediately.

Dr. Prasit is a very friendly and experienced doctor, speaks excellent English, and immediately recognized my problem. After the examination, he used professional instruments to remove a large amount of earwax that had accumulated in front of my ear canal. I'd never experienced anything like it before.

I felt a significant improvement immediately after the treatment. I also received antibiotic ear drops and tablets from the pharmacy and am supposed to come back for a check-up in a week.

Conclusion: Competent, efficient, friendly – ​​highly recommended.

restaurant_name: Dr. Prasit - Ear Nose Throat Clinic
text:
They're living in the future here! Poor France, where I live.

I'll explain how it works for foreigners. You go in and they ask for some kind of ID; I gave them my driver's license or something similar just to complete the paperwork—it's easier than spelling it out.

You're in the waiting room, and your turn comes. Be careful, it's up to you to figure out roughly when it's your turn because I thought they were calling me, so I let several people go ahead until I understood.

Then you see the doctor, who writes his report and sends it to the assistant in the waiting room. She calls you in and gives you the medication that's been prepared for your treatment.
Basically, it took me 30 minutes even though there were at least five or six people ahead of me, and it would have only taken 20 minutes if I'd been seen first. But even if it had taken an hour, I would still have been happy because in France it takes between 3 and 6 months to get an appointment with an ENT specialist. I woke up at 9 a.m., I was in pain, I looked up ENT on Google, and by the time I'd gone there on my scooter and come back, by 11:30 a.m. I was in my hotel room with my medication!

Incredible!
